I'll start by looking at the repo and the docs service.

Reading all of them, including the superseded and draft pages so I can tell them apart.

The errors page came back truncated and the locales page returned 403. I'll retry both.

The pages are all read. Before writing the fix I'll check whether the environment has tz data to help with link-name detection.

Now the rewrite.

The shell call was cut off and nothing ran. I'll make the edits with `edit_file` instead.

The existing test expects a plain space in `USD 1,464.31`, so I'll update it to the no-break space the current rules require. I'll also add tests for the new behaviour.

I rewrote `monthly_statement` in `/app/statements/meridale.py` to follow the current Meridale pages. `cd /app && python -m unittest` passes (3 tests, exit 0). I couldn't check it against a live Meridale server. I ignored the 2025 display rules and the v3 draft.

Each statement now sends one `GET /v2/settlements` with exactly five parameters. The deprecated `lang` and `format` are gone, and `utc_offset` is never sent.

- **Zones:** `tz` is sent as a canonical zone id. Link names such as `US/Eastern` and `Asia/Calcutta` map to their canonical ids. `UTC` and `GMT` become `Etc/UTC`. A stored offset like `UTC-03:00` becomes `Etc/GMT+3`, with the sign inverted, and `UTC+00:00` becomes `Etc/UTC`.
- **Dates:** `from` is the first of the month and `to` is the first of the next month, because the range is half-open. This fixes the missing last day.
- **Locale:** the POSIX name is turned into a supported tag. `pt_BR.UTF-8` becomes `pt-BR`, `es_CL` becomes `es`, and `pt_PT` becomes `en-US`.
- **Rounding:** gross, fees and refunds are read as decimals and rounded half-even to the currency's digits: 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD, 2 otherwise. Net is the difference of the rounded figures, and the total is the sum of the nets.
- **Text:** `net_text` and `total_text` are built locally from the locale's separators, the currency code and a no-break space.

- **Link names:** only the link names in the time-zones page are mapped. Any other stored link name is sent unchanged and would be rejected by the server.
- **Offsets:** an offset that isn't a whole hour raises `ValueError`, since only whole-hour `Etc` zones exist.
- **Existing test:** I changed its expected text from `USD 1,464.31` to use a no-break space, as the current rules require. I also added tests for the request parameters, rounding and text formatting.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.
